issue.title: Gate Rust CI on JavaScript CI, add a parity manifest and agent push-gate rules, and align CI with the pipeline templates

repository.name: relative-meta-logic
repository.description: A prototype for logic framework that can reason about anything relative to given probability of input statements.

issue.body:
## Problem

relative-meta-logic has a JavaScript implementation (`js/src`, about 9k lines in `rml-links.mjs` alone) and a Rust one (`rust/src/lib.rs`, 14k lines). Parity is checked, but the CI/CD does not follow the standard from link-assistant/router#759 or the shared pipeline templates. Rust jobs can start without a green JavaScript stage, there is no parity manifest, there are no agent rules for bulk drafting with a single push, and the usual release, link, security and workflow-lint pipelines are missing. Draft PR #184 (+400,307 lines, 100 commits, open since 2026-09-20) shows the cost: its branch `issue-183-7fedfddffe9c` has 22 failed and 1 cancelled `issue-183-acceptance` runs and 0 green, 5 failed `formal-corpus`, 4 failed `tests`, 7 failed `cache-portability`, 3 failed `orientation-proofs`, and 2 cancelled `tests` runs.

## Findings

1. No gate between the JavaScript and Rust stages. `.github/workflows/tests.yml` has jobs `js` and `rust` side by side with no `needs:`. `parity.yml` builds Rust (`cargo build --bin rml`) in the same job as the JavaScript steps. `docker.yml` builds both. A failing JavaScript job does not stop Rust from starting.
2. Path filters can skip checks. `parity.yml`, `bootstrap.yml` and `docker.yml` run only for listed paths (for example `parity.yml` does not list `scripts/**` other than two files, `lib/**`, or `examples/**`), while `tests.yml` has no filter. Different workflows therefore run on different subsets of changes, and no single required check covers all of them.
3. No branch protection on `main` (`gh api repos/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic/branches/main/protection` returns 404 "Branch not protected"), so nothing makes any stage required.
4. The `parity` workflow (green 15/15 on #184, 26/26 on the branch) verifies only one thing: `scripts/check-corpus-parity.mjs` runs `test-corpus/` through the JS CLI and the Rust `rml` binary and compares stdout and exit status. It is a useful output check, but there is no parity manifest (no file listing each feature with its JavaScript implementation, Rust implementation and evidence), so features that are not in the corpus (LSP, CST, Lean/Rocq export, the `rml-check` and `rml-meta` binaries, the large linked-semantics surface in #184) have no parity check. Because the workflow is green by construction on the corpus, its green status does not tell whether the 13 other checks in #184 pass.
5. Rust is hand-written in parallel with JavaScript, not generated through meta-language. `rust/Cargo.toml` depends on the `meta-language` crate (0.49.0) and `js/package.json` on the npm package (^0.46.0), and the two versions differ. There is no translation step and no regenerate-and-diff check. `rust/src/lib.rs` is 14,205 lines and `js/src/rml-links.mjs` is 9,060 lines kept in sync by hand.
6. `concurrency` is missing in `parity.yml`, `bootstrap.yml`, `docker.yml`, `lint-english.yml`. Only `tests.yml` (cancel on non-main) and `api-docs.yml` have it. With push-per-fix this produces overlapping runs; the branch of #184 has 26 runs of each of these workflows.
7. Rust build load is not configured: `rust/Cargo.toml` has no `[profile.*]` section (no `debug = "line-tables-only"` or `debug = 0`, no `incremental = false` for CI), there is no `.cargo/config.toml`, no `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` or `-j` limit in any workflow, and no artifact pruning. `tests.yml` caches with `Swatinem/rust-cache@v2`, but `parity.yml` and `docker.yml` build Rust without a cache. `rust/Cargo.toml` has no `rust-version`.
8. No agent instructions. The repository has no `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `CONTRIBUTING.md`, so there are no rules for bulk drafting sub-agents and a single push gate. #184 reached 100 commits with many red runs.
9. Differences from the templates (rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template and js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template):
   - Missing workflows: `release.yml` (version, changelog fragments, publish), `links.yml` (lychee link check, no `lychee.toml`), `security.yml`, `workflows.yml` (workflow lint). There is no `changelog.d/` or `CHANGELOG.md`, and no `dependabot.yml` or `renovate` config.
   - Action pinning is inconsistent: `tests.yml` uses `actions/checkout@v6`, but `parity.yml` and `bootstrap.yml` use `@v4` and `setup-node@v4`; none are pinned to a commit SHA.
   - Docker workflows (`docker.yml`) and `api-docs.yml` are the only publish-like flows; the crate (0.19.0) and npm package are never released by CI. This is partly covered by #185.
   - No false-positive/negative guards for CI (for example a check that every workflow's required job still exists).
10. Stale pull request: #184 is the only open PR (draft, open since 2026-09-20, last updated 2026-10-09), a single +400k line change too large to review that has never had a full green run. `main` itself is green (last 30 runs succeeded) but its last run was 2026-07-11.

## Requirements

1. Make Rust CI start only after JavaScript CI passes for the same commit: in `tests.yml` add `needs:` for every JavaScript job (lint, tests, parity, bootstrap, translation check) to the Rust jobs, or use `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha`. Move the `cargo build` out of `parity.yml`'s first stage or make it depend on the JavaScript job. A cancelled, skipped or failed JavaScript run must not start Rust.
2. Remove path filters from the gate jobs (or add an always-run summary job that is skipped-safe) so a Rust-only change still runs the JavaScript, parity and bootstrap checks.
3. Enable branch protection on `main` requiring the JavaScript stage, the Rust stage and parity.
4. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`) listing each feature with its JavaScript and Rust implementation and test evidence, and a checker script run in both the JS and Rust stages that fails when a feature is missing on one side. Cover the CLI, `rml-check`, `rml-meta`, LSP/CST, Lean/Rocq export and the linked-semantics surface of #184, not only `test-corpus/`.
5. Add a translation step from the JavaScript source to Rust through meta-language with a regenerate-and-diff check, or document in `docs/` exactly which parts cannot be translated yet, keep them listed in the manifest, and report each gap to link-foundation/meta-language with a minimal example. Align the `meta-language` versions in `rust/Cargo.toml` and `js/package.json`.
6. Add `concurrency` groups to `parity.yml`, `bootstrap.yml`, `docker.yml` and `lint-english.yml` (cancel in progress for pull requests, not for the Rust stage after the gate, not for `main`).
7. Add a Rust build profile and CI settings: `debug = "line-tables-only"` (or `0`) and `incremental = false` for CI, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, `-j` limited, `Swatinem/rust-cache` in every workflow that builds Rust, a shared bounded `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` for local use, and a documented prune step. Set `rust-version`.
8. Add `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` describing: drafting sub-agents never push; exactly one CI/CD sub-agent pushes, once per batch of fixes for all failures of the last run; no push while a run for the same commits is in progress; JavaScript checks locally, Rust builds locally only for Rust-only changes.
9. Bring the CI in line with the templates: add `release.yml` (changelog fragments in `changelog.d/`, version bump, crates.io and npm publish; coordinate with #185), `links.yml` with `lychee.toml`, `security.yml`, `workflows.yml` (workflow lint), a dependency update config; pin actions to one major version consistently (`checkout@v6`, `setup-node@v6`) or to SHAs. Add a CI check that fails if any workflow can start Rust jobs without the JavaScript gate.
10. Split or land #184 in reviewable pieces, and make `issue-183-acceptance`, `formal-corpus` and `tests` pass or remove them from the required set with a recorded reason. Record before/after numbers (pushes per PR, runs per PR green/failed/cancelled) in `docs/case-studies/`.

## Related

- link-assistant/router#759 (the standard and this audit)
- link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#185 (crate/npm publishing and release workflow; partly covers requirement 9 release flow)
- link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#183 and PR #184 (the red acceptance checks)
- link-foundation/meta-language (translation gaps)

---
We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.

issue.title: Release 1.24.0 stuck in partial-publication, hourly delivery check red since 2026-10-05; no link, workflow-lint or security-scan workflows
issue.body:
## Problem

Router's release health is broken on main and nobody is alerted, and several of the shared template's guards are missing. Release 1.24.0 has been in `partial-publication` for five days, and the hourly delivery check has failed 19 times in a row without opening an issue. The repo has also never had workflow linting, CodeQL, dependency review or a link checker, which `rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` ships. This is separate from #759 (JS-first, push gate, Rust gating).

## Findings

1. **Release 1.24.0 is stuck and the failure is unattended.** `gh run list -w "Merged Source Delivery" --limit 41` on 2026-10-10: 27 failures, 14 successes. The last success was 2026-10-05T07; every run since (19 consecutive, latest run 38011488936) fails. The run's `delivery.json` says `state: partial-publication`, `version: 1.24.0`, `release_stable: false`, `artifacts_verified: false`, `artifact_error: "curl diagnostic failed; inspect saved delivery logs"`. The suggested fix is `gh workflow run release.yml -f release_mode=recover`. Nothing opened an issue or notified anyone; `.github/workflows/delivery.yml` only fails the job and uploads `delivery-state`. The curl diagnostic failure is not explained in the output, so it is not known whether this is a real broken artifact or a false positive in `scripts/check-delivery.rs`.
2. **No workflow linting or workflow security scan.** The template has `.github/workflows/workflows.yml` (actionlint, zizmor, per-job tool-installation check via `scripts/check-workflow-tools.rs`). Router has `scripts/check-workflow-tools.rs` but no workflow that runs actionlint or zizmor; `grep -i -E "actionlint|zizmor|codeql" .github/workflows` finds nothing. `release.yml` is 1,732 lines with 24 `timeout-minutes` entries and many per-job `permissions:` blocks, which is the kind of file where this scanning matters.
3. **No CodeQL and no dependency review.** The template's `security.yml` has Cargo audit, CodeQL (per language) and Dependency Review. Router only runs `cargo audit` inside `release.yml` (job `audit`, lines 341-393). Router also ships Python (610k), JavaScript packages and a `ui/` npm project that no scanner covers. No `deny.toml` or equivalent licence/source policy exists.
4. **No broken-link checking.** The template has `links.yml`, `lychee.toml`, `scripts/check-web-archive.mjs` and `scripts/recheck-broken-links.mjs`. Router has none of them, although `docs/` holds many case studies, provider evidence and integration docs with external URLs.
5. **No repository hygiene files.** There is no `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE` or `.github/pull_request_template.md`. For a credential-handling proxy, a security reporting policy is the most important of these.
6. **Cancelled and red runs on main and the PR branch.** `CI/CD Pipeline` on main: 2 cancelled of 9 in the last 40 runs, even though `release.yml` only cancels pull-request runs (`cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`); `Mutants` and `Real Client Capture` also show cancelled runs on main (`cancel-in-progress: true` in `mutants.yml:43`, `real-clients.yml:19` has no event guard). Several of the other workflows (`benchmarks`, `docker-build`, `fuzz`, `soak`, `upgrade-matrix`, `macos-keychain`) also use unconditional `cancel-in-progress: true`, so a push to main can cancel the previous main run. Only `release.yml` and `bindings.yml` guard on the event. For main, a cancelled verification workflow leaves no result for that commit.
7. **Scheduled and long jobs have no failure reporting.** `fuzz.yml` (daily cron), `delivery.yml` (hourly cron) and `verify-releases.yml` have no step that opens or updates an issue on failure. Finding 1 is the result.

## Requirements

1. Diagnose the 1.24.0 `partial-publication` state: identify what the curl diagnostic is checking, show the error in the job log (not only in a saved file), and either run the documented recovery or fix `check-delivery.rs` if it is a false positive. The next hourly `Merged Source Delivery` run on main must pass.
2. Make `delivery.yml` (and `verify-releases.yml`, `fuzz.yml`) open or update a single tracking issue when they fail on a schedule and close it when they pass again, so that more than two consecutive failures cannot go unnoticed.
3. Add a `workflows.yml` that runs actionlint and zizmor on `.github/**`, plus the existing `scripts/check-workflow-tools.rs`, as a required check. Fix or explicitly allow-list what they report.
4. Add a `security.yml` with CodeQL for Rust, Python and JavaScript, Dependency Review on pull requests, and a scheduled weekly Cargo audit (keep the one in `release.yml` if it gates releases). Add a `cargo-deny` or equivalent licence and source policy.
5. Add `links.yml` and `lychee.toml` from the template with the Web Archive and re-check scripts, scoped to docs paths, and fix or exclude the currently broken links.
6. Add `SECURITY.md`, `CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md`, issue templates and a pull request template, using the template as the starting point.
7. Set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}` (or a per-branch group that never cancels main) on every workflow that runs on `push` to main, and add a check that no main-triggered workflow has unconditional `cancel-in-progress: true`.
8. Report at the end a list of every difference remaining against `rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`, each marked as adopted or intentionally different with a reason.

## Related

- #759 (JS-first, single push gate, Rust gated on JS CI, measurement). This issue does not repeat it. Requirement 7 here is compatible with the per-branch Rust-stage concurrency in #759 requirement 6.
- #745 (full test compilation exhausts a 3 GiB container) already covers build-memory problems; not repeated here.
- #648 and #639 (closed) covered earlier CI false positives and delivery observability; finding 1 shows that delivery is observable but not alerting.
- PR #749 (draft, `CI/CD Pipeline` 7 failures, 3 cancelled, 4 successes of the last 100 runs on the branch) is the visible symptom of the cancel behaviour in #759.
---
We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.

issue.title: Adopt the JavaScript-first, gated CI/CD standard and close the pipeline-template gaps
issue.body:
## Problem

link-assistant/router#759 sets a standard for large Rust projects: JavaScript first with a native implementation at parity, Rust CI/CD gated on green JavaScript CI/CD, bounded Rust build load, single-push-gate agent rules, and the checks from the two pipeline templates and `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`. This repository (about 32.7k lines of Rust in `src/`, plus a React web UI in `web/`) was audited against that checklist on 2026-10-10. The calculator exists only as Rust, the web UI only calls it through WASM, all CI is one Rust-first workflow, and several template workflows and agent rules are absent.

## Findings

1. **No native JavaScript implementation and no parity manifest.** `web/src/worker.ts:15` imports `init, { Calculator, ... } from '@wasm/link_calculator'`. The `web/` package (`link-calculator-web`) has only UI code, hooks and utils; no calculation logic is written in JavaScript. There is no `parity/` manifest and no parity checker in `scripts/`.
2. **No meta-language translation and no regenerate-and-diff check.** Rust in `src/` and `tests/` is hand-written. No workflow or script generates Rust from JavaScript.
3. **No JavaScript stage gates Rust.** `.github/workflows/release.yml` is the only CI workflow. The chain is `detect-changes`, `changelog`, `test` (cargo), `coverage`, then `wasm-build` and `web-build` (lines 374-448). The web tests (`npm test`, line 435) and type check run only after the Rust `lint`, `test` and `coverage` jobs, so JavaScript never runs first. `npm run lint` (ESLint, `web/package.json`) and `npm run test:e2e` (Playwright) are not run in any CI job; Playwright appears only in `update-screenshots.yml:70`. The `scripts/*.test.mjs` tests run inside the Rust `lint` job (line ~55). `push`/`pull_request` use `paths:` filters (lines 4-28), so a change outside the listed paths skips CI entirely.
4. **Push-per-fix waste.** The workflow `concurrency` (lines 54-56) cancels in-progress runs on every non-main ref, including the Rust stage. `gh run list` of 100 recent runs: branch `issue-225-*` had 4 failed, 2 cancelled, 2 green `CI/CD Pipeline` runs; `issue-227-*` (PR #228) 2 failed, 2 green; `issue-234-*` 2 cancelled, 4 green; `issue-229-*` 1 cancelled, 2 green. `release.yml` over its history: 16 failures and 4 cancelled of 100 runs.
5. **Rust build load is unmanaged.** There is no `.cargo/config.toml`. `release.yml` caches `target` together with `~/.cargo/registry` under a key of only `hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock')` (lines 184, 264, 302, 344), with no pruning (`cargo-sweep`, `Swatinem/rust-cache` or equivalent), and sets no `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, no `debug` reduction and no `-j` limit for local agent builds. `cargo test --all-features` builds 55 integration test binaries from `tests/` separately.
6. **No agent instructions.** There is no `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`, and `CONTRIBUTING.md` says nothing about bulk drafting sub-agents, a single push gate or waiting for in-progress runs.
7. **Template differences.** The Rust template has `links.yml` (with `lychee.toml`), `security.yml` and `workflows.yml`; the JS template has the same three. This repository has none of them: no link check, no security scan (no cargo-audit/deny, npm audit, secrets scan or CodeQL anywhere in `.github`, `scripts`, `Makefile` or `.pre-commit-config.yaml`), no workflow linting, and no `.github/dependabot.yml` or `CODEOWNERS`. Actions are pinned by major tag only (`actions/checkout@v6`) and `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable` floats (10 uses).
8. **Sub-issue closing links on PR #228** are tracked separately in #247 and are not repeated here.

Checked and fine: no recent failure on `main` (last failed `release.yml` run on main was 2026-07-16); the only open PR is #228 (created 2026-10-07, not stale); `docs/case-studies/` exists.

## Requirements

1. Add a native JavaScript implementation of the calculator (Node 20+ and Bun, no WASM) and use it in `web/` for the same operations the WASM `Calculator` exposes. Add `parity/*.json` plus a checker script that fails CI if a feature exists in only one language, run by both a JavaScript job and a Rust job.
2. Generate the Rust code from the JavaScript source with link-foundation/meta-language, with a CI step that regenerates and diffs it. Report each untranslatable construct to meta-language with a minimal example and list it in a documented allowlist.
3. Split CI so the JavaScript stage (ESLint, type check, vitest, scripts tests, parity, regenerate-and-diff, and a Playwright smoke test) runs first, and every Rust job `needs:` all of its jobs. Verify with a CI check that fails if a workflow can start a Rust job without this gate. Parity and translation checks must run regardless of `paths:` filters. Required status checks in branch protection must include both stages.
4. Keep `cancel-in-progress` only for the JavaScript stage. The Rust stage uses a per-branch concurrency group without cancellation. Report before/after for runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled) for the next five PRs.
5. Add `.cargo/config.toml` (shared bounded `target-dir` option, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`, reduced `debug`), a cache keyed so `target` does not grow without bound, and pruning of old artifacts in CI and in the documented local workflow. Document that local agent runs execute JavaScript tests by default.
6. Add `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` and a `CONTRIBUTING.md` section: drafting sub-agents never push; one CI/CD sub-agent pushes once after collecting all failures of the latest run and never while a run is in progress on the same commit range.
7. Port from the two templates: `links.yml` with `lychee.toml`, `security.yml` (dependency audit for Cargo and npm, secrets scan), `workflows.yml` (actionlint), Dependabot for cargo, npm and github-actions, and pin third-party actions to commit SHAs (or document why tags are accepted). Pin the Rust toolchain via `rust-toolchain.toml`.

## Related

- link-assistant/router#759 (parent standard, requirement 9)
- #247 (PR #228 closing references), #227 and #235-#246 (feature work; not about CI/CD, no overlap)
- No open issue in this repository covers findings 1-7.

---
We need to download all logs and data related about the issue to this repository, make sure we compile that data to `./docs/case-studies/issue-{id}` folder, and use it to do deep case study analysis (also make sure to search online for additional facts and data), in which we will reconstruct timeline/sequence of events, list of each and all requirements from the issue, find root causes of the each problem, and propose possible solutions and solution plans for each requirement (we should also check known existing components/libraries, that solve similar problem or can help in solutions).

If there is not enough data to find actual root cause, add debug output and verbose mode if not present, that will allow us to find root cause on next iteration.

If issue related to any other repository/project, where we can report issues on GitHub, please do so. Each issue must contain reproducible examples, workarounds and suggestions for fix the issue in code. Also double check to fully apply requirements to entire codebase, so if we have issue in multiple places, it should be fixed in all them.

Please plan and execute everything in this single pull request, you have unlimited time and context, as context auto-compacts and you can continue indefinitely, until it is each and every requirement fully addressed, and everything is totally done.

issue.title: Adopt the JavaScript-first CI gate and the single push gate from router#759 (Rust CI runs ungated, PR #1188 has 0 green CI runs)

repository.name: formal-ai
repository.description: Symbolic first, formal, logical, and data driven associative language processor

issue.body:
## Problem

formal-ai is a big Rust project with a JavaScript and TypeScript implementation. Rust CI/CD starts on every push without waiting for JavaScript checks. The JavaScript gate only parses files. PR #1188 shows the cost: many pushes, almost no green runs. This issue applies the rules from link-assistant/router#759 to this repository.

## Findings

1. **Rust jobs are not gated on JavaScript jobs.** In `.github/workflows/release.yml` the Rust jobs `lint` (line 279), `test` (357, matrix with `cargo test`) and `build` (592) depend only on `detect-changes` and `base`. `coverage.yml` and `layered-ci.yml` also trigger on their own on `pull_request`. No workflow uses `workflow_run`. `layered-ci.yml` orders js, ts and rust tiers only inside itself, and `release.yml` never waits for it.
2. **The JavaScript gate checks syntax only.** The `js` job in `.github/workflows/layered-ci.yml` (lines 89-118) runs `node --check`. The JavaScript tests (`npm run test:web`, `rust/tests/web/*.test.mjs`) run only in `coverage.yml:305` (as coverage) and `links.yml:63`. Both are outside any gate for Rust jobs.
3. **No JS/Rust behaviour parity gate.** The `ts` tier checks that every `.js` file has a `.ts` sibling (file-set parity). No workflow checks a feature manifest or shared golden fixtures between the JavaScript and Rust implementations. `grep parity .github/workflows` finds only `layered-ci.yml`. CONTRIBUTING.md says the "closed js-first loop" is not claimed yet.
4. **Skipped or cancelled upstream tiers let the next tier run.** `layered-ci.yml` lines 124 and 157 accept `needs.js.result == 'skipped'` and `needs.ts.result == 'skipped'` as pass. A path-filtered or cancelled JavaScript stage therefore does not block the Rust tier.
5. **Runs are cancelled by the next push.** `release.yml`, `coverage.yml`, `layered-ci.yml` and others set `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`, so every PR push cancels the Rust jobs. On #1188 (100 commits, +1,410,501/-200,572): `CI/CD Pipeline` 0/11 green (10 failed, 1 cancelled), `Layered CI` 0/12 (10 failed, 2 cancelled), `Coverage` 0/11 (6 failed, 5 cancelled), `Question necessity ratchet` 5/12 green (7 failed).
6. **No required status checks on `main`.** The only ruleset, `protection`, has the rules `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`. It has no `required_status_checks` and no pull request rule (`gh api repos/link-assistant/formal-ai/rulesets`).
7. **No documented single push gate for agents.** CONTRIBUTING.md has "Work in bulk; verify selectively" (~line 510) and "push only after re-reading the issue" but does not name one agent as the only pusher. It does not say to collect all failures of the latest run before one push, or to never push while a run is in progress. There is no `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repository root.
8. **Runner OS is not pinned.** `ubuntu-latest` appears 64 times in 28 workflow files. The shared Rust template uses `ubuntu-24.04` and hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md` requires an explicit label.
9. **Daily scheduled workflow is red.** `Self-development status` failed on `main` on 2026-10-05, 06, 07, 08 and 09 (`gh run list --branch main`). `External Benchmarks` also failed on 2026-10-05.
10. **Stale open pull requests.** #887 (opened 2026-08-01), #652 (2026-07-12), #646 (2026-07-10), #644 and #643 (2026-07-08) are still open.
11. **No measurement.** No document reports pushes per PR, runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, or time to first fully green run for #1188 or a typical PR.

## Requirements

1. Make every Rust job (`lint`, `test`, `build`, coverage, e2e that compile Rust) depend on one JavaScript stage for the same commit. Use `needs:` in one workflow, or `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha` and no own `push`/`pull_request` trigger. Test: a PR with a failing JavaScript test starts zero Rust jobs.

issue.title: Adopt the JavaScript-first CI gate, cross-language parity gate and missing repository hygiene in link-cli

repository.name: link-cli
repository.description: A CLI tool to manipulate links.

issue.body:
## Problem

link-cli has three implementations (C# in `csharp/`, Rust in `rust/`, and a JavaScript/WASM web workbench in `js/`) and one workflow per stack. The workflows do not wait for each other, nothing in CI checks that the C# and Rust implementations stay at parity, `main` has no protection, and the open pull requests are stale or red. This is the audit of link-cli against the standard in link-assistant/router#759 (requirements 3, 4, 6 and 8), the shared pipeline templates and `hive-mind/docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`. Only missing or broken practices are listed.

## Findings

1. **Rust and C# CI/CD are not gated on JavaScript.** `.github/workflows/rust.yml`, `csharp.yml` and `wasm.yml` each trigger on their own `push`/`pull_request` and none has `workflow_run` or a cross-workflow `needs:`. The JavaScript unit tests (`npm run test:js`) run only in `wasm.yml` (line 81), which itself builds the Rust WASM crate. A Rust or C# change starts the full Rust matrix and the C# matrix in parallel with the JavaScript checks. Evidence from the run list: for the Dependabot branch `dependabot/nuget/...` on 2026-10-09 `C# CI/CD Pipeline`, `Dependencies`, `Docs` and `Security` all started at the same second (03:49:35Z).
2. **No parity gate between the implementations.** There is no parity manifest and no checker. The only parity artefacts are one Rust test file (`rust/tests/query_processor_csharp_parity_tests.rs`) and prose in `docs/REQUIREMENTS.md`. Nothing fails CI when a feature changes in C# but not in Rust (or the reverse). The `js/` package is a React/WASM workbench over the Rust crate, and no document states which features it covers. Path filters make this worse: `rust.yml` runs only for `rust/**` and `csharp.yml` only for C# paths, so a one-sided change never triggers the other stack's checks.
3. **`main` is not protected.** `gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/branches/main/protection` returns 404 "Branch not protected", and `gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/rulesets` returns an empty list. No required checks, so a red PR can be merged and the three stages are not enforced.
4. **Eight stale pull requests from 2025 are still open.** #36, #37, #38, #39, #40, #41 (all 2025-09-10), #49 (2025-09-10) and #57 (2025-09-15). They are about 13 months old, none has a CI check result, and each duplicates an open issue (#30-#35, #18, #56, #59, #60). There is no stale policy or workflow that closes or flags them.
5. **The only active PR and the default branch are red.** PR #109 (Dependabot, NuGet group, opened 2026-10-09) fails `C# CI/CD Pipeline`: `LinoProtocolCodecTests.ReferencesAreQuotedOnlyWhenNeeded` and `TextMessagesAreDotStuffed` fail on Windows and in "Simulate Fresh Merge", which reports a semantic merge conflict. The `Dependencies` workflow also failed on `main` on 2026-10-08 and 2026-10-09 (daily scheduled runs) and nobody has acted on it.
6. **Files and workflows from the shared templates are missing.** Compared with `rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template` and `js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`, link-cli has none of: `.github/workflows/workflows.yml` (actionlint with shellcheck), `.github/zizmor.yml` (workflow security lint), `.github/codeql/codeql-config.yml`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `docs/ci-cd/troubleshooting.md`. A grep for `actionlint` and `zizmor` in `.github` and `.pre-commit-config.yaml` finds nothing. `js/` has no ESLint or Prettier configuration and no lint script.
7. **No agent rules or push gate.** There is no `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md` or `.github/CODEOWNERS`, so the single-pusher rule for CI/CD fixes from router#759 requirement 4 is not documented here, and nobody is auto-requested to review.

## Requirements

1. Add a stage gate: the Rust and C# jobs run only after the JavaScript stage (lint, tests, parity check) has succeeded for the same commit, using one entry workflow with `needs:` or `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha`. A cancelled or skipped JavaScript run must not start Rust or C#. Testable: a PR with a failing `npm run test:js` shows no Rust or C# job started.
2. Move `npm run test:js` out of the Rust-dependent `wasm.yml` into a JavaScript stage that does not need `wasm-pack` or Rust, and keep the WASM build in the gated stage.
3. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/features.json`) listing each CLI/library feature with its C#, Rust and JavaScript implementation status and test evidence, plus a checker script that fails when an implementation changes a feature entry without the others. Run it in every stack's workflow with no path filter that can skip it.
4. Add shared golden fixtures that both the C# and the Rust test suites must pass, and a CI job that fails if either suite does not load them.
5. Document in `docs/` which features the `js/` workbench implements and which it delegates to the Rust WASM crate.
6. Enable branch protection or a ruleset on `main` that requires the JavaScript, Rust and C# stage checks and blocks merging when any is red. Testable: `gh api repos/link-foundation/link-cli/branches/main/protection` returns 200.
7. Triage PRs #36-#41, #49 and #57: close them, or rebase and run CI. Add a stale workflow (or equivalent) so PRs idle for more than 60 days are flagged and then closed.
8. Fix or close PR #109 so the NuGet group updates are merged green (or held with a linked issue per the `Dependencies` workflow rules), and make the scheduled `Dependencies` failure on `main` open or update a tracking issue instead of staying silently red.
9. Add `workflows.yml` (actionlint with shellcheck), `.github/zizmor.yml` and the CodeQL config from the templates, and fix any findings they report. Add ESLint and Prettier (or document why not) for `js/`.
10. Add `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md` (or `CLAUDE.md`) and `.github/CODEOWNERS`, including the single-pusher rule: one sub-agent pushes only after all failures of the last run are fixed, and no push happens while a run is in progress on the same branch.
11. Add a CI check (extend `.github/scripts/workflow-policy.test.mjs`) that fails if any workflow can start Rust or C# jobs without the JavaScript gate.

- Existing link-cli issues: none cover CI/CD, gating or parity. #91 (rename), #108 (JS/TS adapter) and #110 (Rust import scaling) are unrelated; #18, #30-#35, #56, #59, #60 are the issues duplicated by the stale PRs in finding 4.

issue.title: Gate non-JS CI/CD on JavaScript, add a JS-first parity gate, fix Java release, and add contributor and agent docs

repository.name: links-notation
repository.description: A way to describe data using references and links.

issue.body:
## Problem

links-notation has 7 language implementations (JS, Rust, Python, Java, Go, C#, PHP) with mature per-language CI (main is green, Rust/JS/Python/Go/C#/PHP releases are published at 0.25.1). But it does not follow the standard from link-assistant/router#759 requirement 9: no language stage waits for JavaScript, there is no JavaScript-first parity gate, the Java package is not on Maven Central, and there is no contributor or agent workflow documentation.

## Findings

1. **No JavaScript gate for the other languages.** `.github/workflows/{rust,go,java,csharp,php,python}.yml` each trigger on their own `push`/`pull_request` path filters. None uses `needs:` on `js.yml` and none uses `workflow_run`. The only `workflow_run` is in `pages.yml`. A change under `rust/**` starts Rust CI and publishing without any JavaScript run. Each workflow has its own `findChanged*Files` path filter, so a non-JS change can skip the JS tests entirely.
2. **Cross-language parity is only partly enforced and not JavaScript-first.** The 7 implementations are hand-written (separate sources in `js/`, `rust/`, `python/`, `java/`, `go/`, `csharp/`, `php/`; no translation or regenerate-and-diff step). `binary-interop.yml` checks only the binary format against `docs/protocol/*.txt` vectors. There is no parity manifest and no shared fixtures for the text parser/formatter: each language has its own tests (for example `js/tests/*.test.js` vs `rust/links-notation/tests/*.rs`, `go/*_test.go`). A feature can land in one language and silently be missing in the others. Only `experiments/issue-282/parity` exists, and it is not wired into CI.
3. **Java is not published, and CI reports it as success.** `java/pom.xml` has version 0.25.1, but https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/github/link-foundation/ returns 404, the Maven Central search for group `io.github.link-foundation` returns 0 results, and `gh release list` shows no `[Java]` release (only Rust/JS/Python/Go/C#/PHP). In the latest main run of `java.yml`, `publishToMavenCentral` is `success` and `publishRelease` is `skipped` (`java.yml` lines 224-233 can set `published=skipped`). A skipped publish is shown as green, so nobody notices the package is missing.
4. **Open PR #204 (Java/Go publishing CI/CD) is stale and conflicting.** Created 2026-01-13, last updated 2026-01-13, mergeable state `dirty`. Other open PRs: #185 (2025-12-13), #170 and #167 (2025-11-30), #80 and #76 (2025-09-10, CI `ACTION_REQUIRED`). All are older than 9 months with no decision (merge, rebase or close).
5. **No branch protection or rulesets.** `gh api repos/link-foundation/links-notation/branches/main/protection` returns 404 "Branch not protected" and the rulesets list is empty. Required checks (JS stage plus the language stages) cannot be enforced.
6. **No contributor or agent workflow docs.** The repository root has no `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` (the rust pipeline template has `CONTRIBUTING.md`). The single-push-gate sub-agent rules and the JavaScript-first rule from #759 are not written down.
7. **No changelog fragments / single release flow.** Root has one `CHANGELOG.md`; there is no `changelog.d` as in the Rust template, and releases are produced by seven independent workflows with separate tags (`js_`, `rust_`, `python_`, `go/v`, `csharp_`), so one change can release some languages and not others.

## Requirements

1. Make every non-JS language workflow (rust, python, java, go, csharp, php) start only after the JS stage succeeded for the same commit. Use either one entry workflow with `needs:` on all JS jobs, or `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha`, with no own `push`/`pull_request` triggers. A cancelled or skipped JS run must not start them.
2. Make the JS lint/test/parity jobs always run (no path filter that can skip them) for every change under any language directory.
3. Add a CI check that fails if any workflow can start non-JS jobs without the JS gate.
4. Add a parity manifest (for example `parity/language-features.json`) listing each feature with its implementation and evidence per language, a checker run in CI, and shared text fixtures (input and expected parse/format output) that all 7 implementations must pass, like the existing `docs/protocol` binary vectors. A new feature must fail CI until all languages (or an explicit documented exception) are updated.
5. Document and enforce JavaScript-first development: features and fixes land in JS first. State in the docs which languages are hand-written and which are generated, and where meta-language translation can be used.
6. Fix Java publishing so the package appears on Maven Central, and add a GitHub release `[Java]`. A skipped or failed publish on a version bump on main must fail the job (or open a visible alert) instead of being green. Verify with `curl https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/io/github/link-foundation/` returning 200 and the version present. Do the same check for each registry in the existing `release-audit` workflow.
7. Resolve each open PR (#204, #185, #170, #167, #80, #76): rebase and merge, or close with a reason. Document the decision in the PR.
8. Enable a branch ruleset for `main` requiring the JS stage and the language checks, with a per-branch `concurrency` group without cancel-in-progress for the gated stages.
9. Add `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` describing the single-push-gate sub-agent workflow (drafting agents never push; one CI/CD agent pushes once after collecting all failures from the latest run; no push while a run is in progress on the same range) and minimal local load (JS tests by default; bounded `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` for Rust).

issue.body:
## Problem

`link-foundation/start` keeps a JavaScript implementation (`js/`, about 16k lines) and a hand-written Rust port (`rust/`, about 21k lines). The standard in link-assistant/router#759 asks for JavaScript first, a behavior-level parity gate, Rust CI/CD gated on green JavaScript CI/CD, bounded Rust build load, and agent rules with a single push gate. The repository has none of the gate, the manifest, the generation check, the build-load settings or the agent rules. Parity is only a test-count heuristic. Main has been green since 2026-09-03, so this is about process, not a broken pipeline.

## Findings

1. **Rust CI/CD is not gated on JavaScript CI/CD.** `.github/workflows/rust.yml` and `.github/workflows/js.yml` are separate workflows. Both trigger on `push` to main and on `pull_request` (rust.yml lines 3-30). No workflow uses `workflow_run`, and no Rust job has a `needs:` on a JavaScript job. Each workflow has its own path filter (`js/**` versus `rust/**`), so a change to one language never runs the other stage. A branch can run the Rust matrix (`test` on several OS, `coverage`, `build`) while JavaScript is red or still running.
2. **Parity is a test-count heuristic, not behavior parity.** `scripts/check-test-parity.mjs` greps `it(` in `js/test` and `#[test]` / `fn test_` in `rust/`, and fails only if Rust has 10% fewer tests. It runs only in `rust.yml` (job `test-parity`, line 368). There is no parity manifest, no per-feature list with JavaScript and Rust evidence, no shared fixtures or golden tests, and no JavaScript-side job that fails when Rust changes alone.
3. **Rust is not generated from JavaScript.** `rg meta-language` finds no match in the repository. Rust is maintained by hand, so there is no regenerate-and-diff check and no list of constructs that cannot be translated yet.
4. **No Rust build-load controls.** `rust/Cargo.toml` has no `[profile.*]` section, there is no `.cargo/config.toml`, and `CARGO_INCREMENTAL`, `-j` limits and `cargo-sweep` / pruning appear nowhere in the workflows. The cache step (rust.yml lines 256 and 308, repeated in `coverage` and `build`) stores `rust/target` keyed only by `hashFiles('rust/Cargo.lock')` with a broad `restore-keys` fallback, so old artifacts carry over into each new cache and grow without a bound. There are three Rust test OS legs plus a tarpaulin coverage build, each compiling the crate separately.
5. **No agent or contributor instructions.** `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` do not exist (the Rust template ships `CONTRIBUTING.md`). Nothing describes bulk drafting sub-agents, a single push owner, or running only JavaScript checks locally.
6. **Push-per-fix waste is visible.** On recent PR branches: `issue-195-cd307f03a9cf` had 2 failed `JavaScript CI/CD`, 2 failed `Rust CI/CD` and 1 failed `Workflows` run before the merge; `issue-183-4cba24615d2f` had 2 failed JavaScript runs, 1 cancelled Rust run and 1 cancelled Security run. Across the last 300 runs, 18 are cancelled and 51 failed on non-main branches (169 succeeded). Every job uses `cancel-in-progress: true`, including on `main`, while the templates use `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}`.
7. **No branch protection.** `gh api repos/link-foundation/start/branches/main/protection` returns "Branch not protected", so neither stage is a required check.

Verified fine, not findings: actions pinning follows `.github/zizmor.yml` policy, link check, security and workflow lint exist, main CI has been green since 2026-09-03, and no pull requests are open. There are no open issues.

## Requirements

1. Make every Rust job wait for JavaScript. Either add Rust jobs to one entry workflow with `needs:` on all JavaScript jobs, or trigger `rust.yml` only through `workflow_run` with `conclusion == 'success'` and the same `head_sha`, with no `push` or `pull_request` triggers of its own. A cancelled, skipped or failed JavaScript run must not start Rust.
2. Remove path filters that let a Rust-only change skip the JavaScript gate: the parity and translation checks must always run.
3. Add `parity/features.json` listing each feature with its JavaScript and Rust implementation and test evidence, plus a checker run by both `js.yml` and `rust.yml` that fails when one side changes without the other. Keep `check-test-parity.mjs` only as a secondary signal.
4. Add shared fixtures or golden tests that both implementations must pass for CLI parsing, isolation arguments, status output and the execution record format.
5. Generate the Rust code from JavaScript with link-foundation/meta-language, or document per construct what cannot be translated yet (with issues in meta-language). Add a regenerate-and-diff CI check, and keep hand-written Rust small and listed in the manifest.
6. Add `[profile.dev]` / `[profile.test]` settings with reduced debug info, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0` in CI, a bounded shared `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` for local use, and pruning (`cargo-sweep` or a cache key that does not restore stale artifacts). Document local limits (`-j`, memory).
7. 8. Use `cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}` as the templates do, so runs on main are never cancelled, and use a per-branch group without cancel for the gated Rust stage.
9. Enable branch protection on `main` requiring the JavaScript and Rust stage checks.
10. Add a CI check that fails if any workflow can start Rust jobs without the JavaScript gate, and report before/after pushes per PR and cancelled/failed runs per PR.

issue.title: Make CI on main green and enforced, validate before push, and generate Rust from JavaScript instead of writing it twice
issue.body:
## Problem

meta-language is the translator that other Rust projects are meant to use to get Rust from JavaScript (link-assistant/router#759). It applies that standard to itself only in part. The JavaScript/Rust parity gate and the `js` -> `rust` job order in `ci.yml` exist and work. But the Rust code is still mostly written by hand next to the JavaScript, the `CI` workflow has no green run on any branch including `main`, nothing requires it to pass before a merge, and pushes are not checked locally, so each CI failure is found one push at a time.

## Findings

1. **Rust is written twice by hand; only one module is generated.** `rust/src` has 122,747 lines of Rust and `js/src` has 48,042 lines of JavaScript. The only Rust generated from JavaScript with a regenerate-and-diff check is `rust/src/translation/frontend_rules.rs` (534 lines; `npm run check:frontend-rules`, see `docs/self-translation.md`). The per-module `Self-Translation Report` (8 shards in `ci.yml`) only measures how far the translation is from the hand-written Rust. It does not fail when the two differ and does not make the Rust come from the translation.
2. **`CI` has no green run on any branch, including `main`.** Of the last 100 `CI` runs, 0 succeeded (`gh run list --workflow CI`): `main` 3/3 failed (2026-10-06, 2026-10-08 x2), `issue-195-*` 0/28, `issue-199-58f3573d6122` (PR #201, draft, +134,131/-5,667, 58 commits, open since 2026-10-07) 0/44 (25 failed, 19 cancelled), `issue-199-679a3b3c3c56` 0/11, `issue-202-203-*` 0/9, `issue-217-*` 0/5. PR #216 was merged into `main` while `CI` was red (head `eb0574d`, run 37799195371: `Post-merge Report` and `Full Requirements Aggregate` failed, `issue-195: 310/323 requirements passed`).
3. **Nothing requires green CI to merge.** `GET /repos/link-foundation/meta-language/branches/main/protection` returns 404. The only ruleset, `safety`, has the rules `deletion` and `non_fast_forward`; it has no required status checks and no pull request rule. `Full Requirements Aggregate` is described in `ci.yml` as "a required check", but it is not required by any rule.
4. **The failures are different on each run and are found only in CI.** Run 37998880234 (PR #201, 2026-10-09 22:24): `JavaScript Tests (grammar)` failed on `the native Go fixture is current` (`parity/fixtures/native-grammars/go.json is stale; run node scripts/generate-native-grammar-fixtures.mjs`), and `JavaScript Package` failed on the same stale-fixture check (`npm run check:native-grammars`). Run 37984660603: `not ok 262 - native Python matches the independent oracle on every pinned upstream corpus input`. Run 37939535878: that Python test plus `not ok 50 - formal-ai regression: every JavaScript documents entry digests to the Rust golden`. A stale generated file is a one-command local check, yet it failed the whole run. The hook in `.githooks/pre-commit` only cleans caches; there is no `pre-push` hook or documented command that runs `npm run check` and the grammar test group before a push.
5. **No single push gate, and every new push cancels the running stage.** `ci.yml` uses `cancel-in-progress: true` for pull requests at the workflow level and in every job (lines 27-29, 193-195, ...); `js.yml` and `rust.yml` do the same for the Rust stage. 19 of the 44 runs on PR #201 were cancelled before finishing. `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md` do not describe a rule that drafts are bulk and only one agent pushes after collecting all failures of the last run (they only set `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`).
6. **No workflow-gate check.** `ci.yml` makes `rust` depend on `js` (`needs: [changes, js]`), but nothing fails if a later edit lets a Rust job start without the JavaScript stage. Also, the `changes` job skips the Rust workflow for JavaScript-only changes through a path filter (`ci.yml` lines 40-57); this is acceptable only because the JavaScript stage has the parity check, and that dependency is not tested.
7. **Template workflows are missing.** Compared with link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template, `.github/workflows` has no `links.yml` (link check), `security.yml`, or `workflows.yml` (workflow lint), and the repository has no `.github/zizmor.yml`, `.github/codeql/`, `.lycheeignore` or `.github/dependabot.yml`. Only `secretlint` runs (`js.yml:275`, `rust.yml:164`). No workflow runs `actionlint`, `zizmor`, CodeQL, `cargo audit` or `cargo deny`.
8. **No measurement.** There is no before/after report of pushes per PR, runs per PR (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, time to first fully green run, or local peak RSS/disk (router#759 requirement 7).

## Requirements

1. Make `CI` on `main` green and keep it green: fix the causes in findings 2 and 4 (stale `parity/fixtures/native-grammars/go.json`, the native Python oracle test, the formal-ai documents digest, the `issue-195` acceptance count). Done when the last 3 `CI` runs on `main` are `success`.
2. Add a ruleset or branch protection for `main` that requires `Full Requirements Aggregate` (and the pull request rule). A pull request with a failed or cancelled `CI` run must not be mergeable. Done when `gh api repos/link-foundation/meta-language/rulesets` lists a `required_status_checks` rule.
3. Generate Rust from JavaScript. Publish in `parity/` a list of modules that are generated (starting with `frontend_rules.rs`) and extend it module by module; each generated module has a `--check` regenerate-and-diff command in `npm run check` and is marked as generated in the Rust file. Make the `Self-Translation Report` fail when a module listed as generated differs from its translation. Hand-written Rust that has no generated counterpart is listed in the parity manifest with the translator issue that blocks it (#204-#213, #219, #220 and others).
4. Add a local pre-push check (a `.githooks/pre-push` installed by `scripts/install-dev-hooks.mjs`, plus one documented command) that runs every `--check` script in `npm run check` and the test groups that touched files affect. Done when the stale `go.json` case fails locally.
5. Document the push gate in `AGENTS.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`: drafting agents never push; one agent pushes once after collecting all failures of the last finished run; no push while a run on the same branch is in progress; JavaScript checks run locally and Rust builds locally only for Rust-only changes. Use a shared bounded `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`.
6. Stop cancelling a Rust stage that has started: for pull requests, `cancel-in-progress` is true only for the JavaScript stage or a queued Rust stage not yet started; a Rust run that passed its gate finishes. Done when a push during a Rust run does not leave a `cancelled` Rust job.
7. Add a CI check (script in `js/scripts`, run in the JavaScript stage) that parses `.github/workflows/*.yml` and fails if any Rust job can start without `needs:` on the JavaScript jobs, or if a path filter can skip the parity and translation checks.
8. Add the missing template workflows and files (`links.yml`, `security.yml` with `zizmor`/CodeQL/dependency audit, `workflows.yml` with `actionlint`, `.github/zizmor.yml`, `.lycheeignore`, `.github/dependabot.yml` for GitHub Actions) or document in `docs/ci-cd/` why a file is not needed.
9. Add `docs/case-studies/` data for PR #201 and `main`: pushes, runs (green/failed/cancelled), CI minutes, time to first green run, and the same numbers after requirements 1-7.

## Related

- link-assistant/router#759 (standard for big Rust projects; this repository is the translator and the first adopter)
- #199 (remaining #195 scope including self-translation) and PR #201 (the red branch)
- #204, #205, #206, #207, #208, #209, #210, #211, #212, #213, #214, #215, #217, #219, #220 (translator gaps that keep Rust hand-written; requirement 3 depends on them, but none covers the gate, the lists, or the checks)
- #197 (dependency freshness in CI, partly covers finding 7)
- link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template (workflow files in finding 7)

## Requirement 9: audits filed

Each repository was audited against this issue, the two pipeline templates and hive-mind `docs/CI-CD-BEST-PRACTICES.md`. Findings already covered by open issues were left out and cross-referenced. The key claims were re-checked with `gh` before filing.

| Repository | Issue | Headline findings |
|---|---|---|
| link-assistant/router | link-assistant/router#760 | Release 1.24.0 stuck in partial publication; delivery check failed 20 of its last 25 runs on `main` (last success 2026-10-05) with no alert; no link check, workflow lint, CodeQL, dependency review or cargo-deny; no SECURITY.md or templates |
| link-foundation/meta-language | link-foundation/meta-language#221 | `CI`: 0 green in the last 100 runs (54 failed, 46 cancelled), `main` red; the ruleset requires no checks; Rust is mostly hand-written (122,747 lines vs 48,042 JS); no pre-push validation or push gate. The JS→Rust `needs:` gate and the parity gate already work. |
| link-foundation/relative-meta-logic | link-foundation/relative-meta-logic#187 | JS and Rust jobs run in parallel with no gate; `main` unprotected; parity is corpus output only; meta-language versions differ (crate 0.49.0, npm ^0.46.0); no release, link or security pipelines; #184 acceptance 0 of 23 green |
| link-assistant/formal-ai | link-assistant/formal-ai#1191 | Rust jobs ungated; the "js" tier is `node --check` only; Layered CI passes `skipped`; the ruleset has no required checks; `Self-development status` red on `main` every day from 2026-10-04 to 2026-10-09; PR #1188 0 green |
| link-foundation/link-cli | link-foundation/link-cli#111 | Rust, C# and WASM ungated; no parity across three implementations; `main` unprotected; 8 stale 2025 PRs; #109 red |
| link-foundation/links-notation | link-foundation/links-notation#339 | Six language workflows ungated; 7 hand-written implementations with no shared fixtures; Java publish reports success but Maven Central has 0 artifacts; `main` unprotected; 6 stale PRs |
| link-foundation/start | link-foundation/start#197 | `rust.yml` not gated on `js.yml`; parity is a test-count heuristic; no cargo build-load settings; no agent or contributor docs; `main` unprotected |
| link-assistant/calculator | link-assistant/calculator#254 | No native JS implementation (the web UI calls WASM only); `release.yml` is the only CI and runs Rust first; ESLint and e2e not in CI; template gaps |

Common gaps across almost all of them: no JavaScript gate in front of Rust, no required status checks on `main`, no data-driven parity manifest (meta-language has one), hand-written Rust instead of meta-language translation, and no agent rules for bulk drafting with a single push gate.
